results.summary: This project is a placeholder for a power-gated test design that was intended as preliminary work for supporting power-gated designs on later IHP shuttles. The documentation states that the pins and behavior are to be filled in later, and the author's silicon report confirms that the power gating experiments did not end up on the shuttle. No functional design was implemented, so there is nothing to test or use. The project is notable only as a reserved but unused slot.

This project is a gate-level Verilog design that was originally intended for FPGA implementation but was later adapted for a multi-tile ASIC. It includes a scan-chain for testing, a reconfigurable logic block, and a finite state machine with a clock generator. The design is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating gate-level design techniques. The documentation is sparse, and the design is not fully verified.

This project is a latch-based design that was originally intended for FPGA implementation but was later adapted for a multi-tile ASIC. It includes a scan-chain for testing, a reconfigurable logic block, and a power-gating feature. The design is not fully verified and the documentation is sparse. The project is notable for its use of latches and power-gating techniques.

This project is a radio modulator that uses a comparator, resistor bias network, RC network, RF amplifier, and an SPI microcontroller to set the station. It includes a demodulator, DSP, and NCO for signal processing. The design is intended for communication applications. The documentation is sparse, but the external hardware requirements are described.

KianV RISC-V RV32E Baremetal SoC is a bare-metal RV32E RISC-V system-on-chip with a UART, a QSPI memory controller for PSRAM and flash, a generic SPI interface, a sigma-delta audio emulator and PWM output. It is designed for embedded applications and can be programmed via the UART or SPI. The SoC includes a memory controller for external PSRAM and flash. It is notable for its small footprint and bare-metal operation.

This One Bit PUF design contains an array of one-bit physical unclonable function cells, addressed by four input pins, that output eight PUF bits selected by the address. The documentation is brief and does not describe the PUF cell implementation or provide silicon test results. The design is intended for security applications. The documentation is too thin to say more about the implementation or its behavior.

This project is a VGA graphics design that includes a clock generator, FSM, and display output. It is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating VGA signal generation. The design is not fully verified and the documentation is sparse. The project is notable for its use of VGA and graphics output.

This project is a PUF-based security design that includes a PRNG, register file, and crypto functionality. It is intended for hardware security applications. The documentation is sparse and does not describe the implementation in detail. The design is notable for its use of PUF technology.

This project is a PUF cell design that is intended for security applications. The documentation consists only of an image and a note that the output is zero in the reset condition, and it does not describe the PUF cell or how to read it. The documentation is too thin to say more about the implementation or its behavior. The design is notable for its use of PUF technology.
